name: laptop32
title: The reader lab: one platform host and seven nested virtual machines
description: Where Nano runs each package. Nano runs ON the platform host - that is where a reader sits, and the seven virtual machines are the thing they are building. So 'lab-host' is this machine, and the estate is one hop away on the management network. There is no jump host and no bastion here: if you are running Nano somewhere else, you do not want this file.
address_plan: The ebook's fixed lab address plan. lab-mgmt 10.100.99.0/24, lab-storage-fe 10.200.99.0/24, lab-storage-be 10.201.99.0/24. These are not secrets; they are the same addresses printed in the deployment guide.
honesty: Nothing in this file is a credential. It names hosts, a user and the PATH to a private key. The key itself stays on your disk and never enters a package, a record or a report.

lab-host.note: The physical machine. Nano runs here, so its commands need no transport at all.

mgmt-01.note: CloudStack management server and its MySQL.

ceph-01.note: Ceph bootstrap node - cephadm runs from here.

ceph-02.note: Ceph node, joined by the cluster package rather than targeted directly.

ceph-03.note: Ceph node, joined by the cluster package rather than targeted directly.

kvm-02.note: Second compute host. Two are mandatory, not optional.

known_hosts_note: Nano keeps its own known_hosts under ~/.matrixclaw-nano/ rather than editing yours. It matters here: rebuilding the estate mints fresh host keys for the same seven addresses, and a stale entry in your own file would fail every connection with a warning about a changed key. Delete Nano's file when you tear the estate down; you cannot break your own SSH by doing it.
